Understanding Graph Matchings

An example of mathematical writing, proofs and diagrams.

← All writing

This is a sample article, included to show how mathematical writing will appear on the website. Replace it with your own work when ready.

Consider a bipartite graph G=(U∪V,E)G=(U\cup V,E)G=(U∪V,E). A matching is a set of edges in which no two edges share a vertex.

A maximum matching MMM has the largest possible size:

∣M∣=max⁡{∣M′∣:M′ is a matching in G}.|M|=\max\{ |M'|:M'\text{ is a matching in }G\}.∣M∣=max{∣M′∣:M′ is a matching in G}.

Algorithm sketch

M ← empty matching
while an augmenting path P exists:
    M ← M △ E(P)
return M
